# Mudate — Portal Inmobiliario Argentina | Argentine Real Estate Portal

> Encontrá propiedades en venta y alquiler en toda Argentina. Casas, departamentos, terrenos y más en Córdoba, Buenos Aires, Mendoza, Rosario y todo el país.
> Find properties for sale and rent across Argentina. Houses, apartments, land and more in Córdoba, Buenos Aires, Mendoza, Rosario and beyond.

Mudate es el portal inmobiliario especializado en el mercado de bienes raíces de Argentina. Ofrecemos datos reales de precios, análisis de rentabilidad y guías para compradores e inversores locales e internacionales.

Mudate is an Argentine real estate portal with over 850 properties across 22+ cities. We provide real pricing data, investment analysis, and guides for both local and international buyers.

## Key Facts / Datos clave

- **Properties listed / Propiedades publicadas:** 850+
- **Cities covered / Ciudades cubiertas:** 22+ (Buenos Aires, Córdoba, Rosario, Mendoza, Salta, Neuquén, Bariloche, and more)
- **Provinces / Provincias:** All major Argentine provinces
- **Currency / Moneda:** USD and ARS (Argentine Peso)
- **Operations / Operaciones:** Venta (sale) and Alquiler (rental)
- **Languages / Idiomas:** Español (Spanish) and English
- **URL:** https://mudateargentina.com

## Argentine Real Estate Market Data (2025–2026)

### National Overview
- Properties in Argentina trade primarily in USD (residential) and ARS (commercial/rental)
- Average USD price per m² in Buenos Aires Capital: USD 2,200–2,800
- Average USD price per m² in Córdoba Capital: USD 1,200–1,400
- Average cap rate nationally: 4–7% USD annually
- Argentina's housing deficit: estimated 3.5 million units nationally
- Real estate is traditionally used as a store of value against peso inflation

### Key Markets

#### Buenos Aires Capital (CABA)
Capital federal with 3 million inhabitants. Premium market with highest prices nationally.
- Average m² price: USD 2,400–2,800 (Palermo, Puerto Madero)
- Cap rate: 3–4% USD annually
- Key neighborhoods: Palermo, Recoleta, San Telmo, Puerto Madero, Almagro

#### Gran Buenos Aires (GBA)
Three zones covering 13 million people:
- **GBA Norte** (Tigre, San Isidro, Vicente López): USD 1,800–2,200/m²
- **GBA Oeste** (Morón, La Matanza): USD 800–1,200/m²
- **GBA Sur** (Quilmes, Lanús): USD 700–1,000/m²

#### Córdoba Capital
Second city of Argentina, capital of Córdoba province. 1.4 million inhabitants.
- Average m² price: USD 1,200–1,400
- Cap rate: 4.5–6% USD annually
- Key areas: Nueva Córdoba (student zone), General Paz, Güemes, Valle Escondido
- 200,000+ university students (UNC, UTN, UCC) sustain rental demand

#### Villa María (Córdoba province)
100,000 inhabitants, second city in Córdoba province.
- Average m² price: USD 900–1,100
- Cap rate: 6.5–7.5% USD (best in province)
- Strong university market (UNVM, 15,000 students)
- 40% cheaper than Córdoba Capital with higher returns

#### Villa Carlos Paz (Córdoba province)
Top tourist destination in Argentina's interior.
- Average m² price: USD 1,400–1,800
- Tourist rental cap rate: 7–10% USD annually
- 3 million tourists annually, Lago San Roque

#### Rosario (Santa Fe)
Third city of Argentina. 1.2 million inhabitants.
- Average m² price: USD 1,400–1,800
- Cap rate: 4–5% USD annually

#### Mendoza
Wine capital of South America. Gateway to Andes.
- Average m² price: USD 1,100–1,500
- Strong foreign investment from wine/tourism industries
- Cap rate: 5–6% USD annually

#### Salta
Colonial city in Northwest Argentina.
- Average m² price: USD 900–1,300
- Growing tourism market
- Cap rate: 5–7% USD annually

#### Bariloche (Río Negro)
Patagonian ski and lake resort.
- Average m² price: USD 1,800–2,500
- Strong seasonal rental demand (ski + summer)
- Cap rate: 5–8% USD annually (highly seasonal)

#### Neuquén
Capital of Neuquén province, oil and gas hub (Vaca Muerta).
- Average m² price: USD 1,200–1,600
- High demand from oil sector workers
- Cap rate: 6–7% USD annually

## Property Types / Tipos de propiedad

- **Departamentos / Apartments** — most common in cities, highest rental demand
- **Casas / Houses** — single-family homes, suburban areas and gated communities
- **Terrenos / Land** — for residential and commercial development
- **Locales comerciales / Commercial** — retail and office spaces
- **Cabañas / Cabins** — tourist properties in Córdoba, Bariloche, Salta
- **PH (Planta Baja)** — ground-floor apartments with private garden
- **Duplex** — two-floor apartments

## Investment Guide / Guía de inversión

### Why invest in Argentine real estate?
1. Properties trade in USD, hedging against peso devaluation
2. Cap rates (4–10%) higher than developed markets
3. Argentina's housing deficit means structural demand
4. Córdoba and interior cities offer best price-to-return ratio
5. Legal framework protects property rights even during economic crises

### Legal process for foreigners
- Foreigners can buy property in Argentina without residency
- Requires CDI (tax ID for foreigners, free to obtain)
- Purchase in USD cash or bank transfer
- Escritura (title deed) process: 30–60 days
- Approximate transaction costs: 3–5% of purchase price (notary, taxes, agents)

### Cap rate comparison (2025)
| Zone | Price USD/m² | Monthly Rent | Cap Rate |
|------|-------------|-------------|---------|
| Buenos Aires Capital | 2,400 | USD 700 | 3.5% |
| Córdoba Capital | 1,300 | USD 600 | 5.5% |
| Villa María | 950 | USD 550 | 6.9% |
| Villa Carlos Paz (tourist) | 1,600 | USD 1,200 (seasonal) | 9% |
| Rosario | 1,500 | USD 600 | 4.8% |
| Mendoza | 1,300 | USD 650 | 6% |
| Bariloche (seasonal) | 2,200 | USD 1,500 (seasonal) | 8.2% |

## About Mudate / Sobre Mudate

Mudate (Spanish for "move/relocate") was founded to fill a gap in the Argentine real estate market: no portal combined quality editorial data, investment analysis, and modern technology for the interior of the country.

Initial focus on Córdoba (best price-to-return ratio in Argentina), now expanded to cover all major Argentine markets.

Target users:
- Argentine families looking to buy or rent
- Local investors seeking USD-denominated returns
- International buyers (expats, diaspora) looking for Argentine real estate
- Real estate professionals and developers
